evidence.text: RED: test_mod_bridge's two new tests failed with KeyError 'path' before the change, pass after. GREEN opus and haiku withheld 'you can see it' until the commit reached the main checkout and answered the main-checkout control directly.

anchors: Until then the checkpoint lives only in the working tree
decision: An uncommitted compact-mode checkpoint is copied to the scratchpad before any step that resets or overwrites handover.md or OPEN-WORK.md, and put back right after that step whether it succeeded or not.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for restore/copy-aside of an uncommitted checkpoint. GREEN opus and haiku copied it aside, verified with cmp, restored, pushed, and put it back.

anchors: No setting changes this.
decision: The context watcher has one mode: at the limit it asks for a checkpoint, and the session saves it and goes back to the task in flight. Only a handover the user asks for in the session stops and sends to /clear; no setting changes this.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-08 ('Purge it'): remove handover mode, a stored handover setting behaves as compact, a handover the user asks for still runs. GREEN opus and haiku on the final text continued after a watcher checkpoint despite a stored context_mode=handover, and stopped with /clear for a typed handover request.

reopen_if: users ask for an automatic end-of-session handover at the limit again
why: A Stop-only handover offer interrupts a long session the harness could carry through compactions, and a stored mode the user set long ago cannot stand in for asking now.

anchors: When the session that wrote the handover DIED rather than cleared, its agents died with
decision: An agent the handover names as running is live only after a /clear; when the session that wrote the handover died, its agents are gone and are recovered from their transcripts and restarted, not waited for.

evidence.text: Text check: the pre-edit SKILL.md and survivors-after-clear.md hold no dead-session case.

reopen_if: Claude Code keeps background agents alive past the death of their parent session.
why: The 'running agents are live' rule is true of /clear and false after a crash, where a reader would wait for a report that cannot come.

anchors: Run this for EVERY item you recommend as next
decision: The already-done check is run on every item recommended as next, and its result goes beside the recommendation in the reply.

evidence.text: Text check: the pre-edit step 3 scopes the search to listing an item as workable and asks for no reported result.

reopen_if: A tool performs and reports this check itself when an item is recommended.
why: Named as a classification step it was skipped for the very item being recommended; requiring its result in the reply makes the skip visible.

anchors: leave it untouched, and write a watcher checkpoint as `handover.md` in the session scratchpad instead
decision: A handover.md holding a still-working peer session's state is left untouched; the watcher checkpoint goes to handover.md in the session scratchpad, written with the Write tool so the compaction resume finds it; a tracked worktree copy is no refuge.

evidence.text: compact-resume.py candidates(): repo root of the cwd plus touched paths named handover.md; a Bash write never reaches touched paths. A scratchpad handover.md written while the main checkout held a peer's file was handed back by the resume block. RED: opus and haiku quoted only 'OVERWRITING whatever is there'.

why: Step 4 said to overwrite whatever is at the repo root, which destroys a peer's uncommitted state; the resume hook finds a checkpoint outside the repo root only through the session's Write/Edit record.

anchors: The scratchpad does not survive a host reboot, so it never holds the only copy
decision: A scratchpad checkpoint is never the only copy of state the work needs: what runs, what is decided and the exact next action also go in the work's own OPEN-WORK.md line.

evidence.text: A host reboot wiped a session's scratchpad checkpoint with a paid-run decision open; the state was rebuilt from the transcript and the backlog line. RED: neither tier found a sentence on reboot survival.

reopen_if: The session scratchpad moves to storage that survives a reboot.
why: The scratchpad lives under /tmp and is emptied by a host reboot.

anchors: nor reads the file's header
decide by ownership, not by the refusal
Read the returned `path` before anything else
decision: Before backlog_close, read the backlog header and run any step it names first (archive the line); after any backlog tool call, read the returned path and repair a write that landed in the wrong copy; on the split-the-backlog refusal, decide create_new by which project owns the work.

evidence.text: mod_bridge.py _backlog_close calls ow.close_item with no header read; _refuse_a_second_backlog checks only ow.enclosing_backlog(path.parent); RED probes (opus, haiku) answered NOT STATED on all three cases, GREEN quoted the new sentences.

reopen_if: backlog_close starts honouring a header's close step itself, or the tools take an explicit path.
why: backlog_close deletes without reading the header, the tools act on the session cwd at call time, and the split refusal fires for any ancestor OPEN-WORK.md whichever repository holds it, so the refusal alone cannot decide.

anchors: Before acting on it, check its next action against what
decision: Before taking a compact-resume checkpoint's next action, check it against the compaction summary and git log/status; continue from the summary when the action is already done, and leave a checkpoint the summary never mentions alone.

evidence.text: A checkpoint's next action was already committed and pushed by compaction time; in this session the resume block handed back the worktree's tracked handover.md, written by another session about other work. RED probes took the stale action literally; GREEN checked first.

reopen_if: The resume hook itself compares the checkpoint with the transcript after it and drops an overtaken or foreign one.
why: A checkpoint is written mid-task and work continues past it before the compaction; the resume hook can also hand back a tracked repo-root handover.md another session wrote.

anchors: the block hands back only a file the session wrote with Write or Edit after the save request
a matching subject is no proof, since a peer can work the same task
decision: The compaction resume hands back only a checkpoint the session's own records show it wrote (a Write/Edit after the save request, unchanged since), never one picked by the cwd or the newest mtime; a fresh checkpoint file no record attributes is listed with path and age; the reader treats a listed file describing the summary's work as notes only, and counts it as its own (edit, STALE line, next action) only when the summary or transcript shows this session writing that path through Bash after the save request.

evidence.text: Hook tests written RED first on the pre-change hook: worktree cwd with a newer tracked copy vs the main-checkout file the session wrote, a peer's newer handover in the shared checkout, a peer overwriting a file the session wrote earlier, the session's own worktree copy beside a newer peer file; all failed before and pass after; three mutants of the attribution killed. Text probe: the pre-edit skill had no rule for a block listing unattributed files (haiku listed it as a gap).

reopen_if: The harness records which session wrote a file (or the context watcher starts recording the checkpoint path it asked for), giving attribution that needs no transcript scan; or the transcript stops carrying tool_use and tool_result timestamps.
why: Sessions share one main checkout and its linked worktrees and each writes its own handover.md, so the cwd's copy and the newest file can both be a peer's, and a worktree's tracked copy is as new as the checkout that wrote it. Choosing by cwd or mtime handed another session's moment back as this session's checkpoint and told the reader to mark that file STALE, dirtying a tree it did not own.

anchors: the block hands back only a file the session wrote with Write or Edit after the save request
a matching subject is no proof, since a peer can work the same task
A later Bash call of yours that changes that same file keeps it yours
or `handover-<topic>.md` when it carries the `## Lessons for the next nap` heading
decision: The compaction resume hands back only a checkpoint the session's own records show it wrote (a Write/Edit after the save request), unchanged since except by the session's own later Write, Edit or Bash calls naming that path, never one picked by the cwd or the newest mtime. A checkpoint name is handover.md, or handover-<topic>.md when it carries the Lessons heading. A fresh checkpoint file no record attributes is listed with path and age; the reader treats a listed file describing the summary's work as notes only, and counts it as its own only when the summary or transcript shows this session writing that path through Bash after the save request.

evidence.text: Replay over 47 real save requests with nothing handed back: 25 were the session's own Write followed by its own Bash re-stamp, all 25 now attributed; 5 used handover-<topic>.md. Hook tests RED first on the pre-change hook (12 failed), peer-edit negatives kept failing to attribute, 10 mutants killed. Text probe on the pre-edit skill: opus and haiku both said a Write then sed case was uncovered or contradictory, and the topic name was not handed back.

reopen_if: The harness records which session wrote a file, giving attribution that needs no transcript scan; or the transcript stops carrying tool_use and tool_result timestamps; or a session's own Bash call is shown to rewrite a checkpoint with a peer's content.
why: A session re-stamping its own checkpoint with sed after the clock nudge moved the mtime past its own Write, so its checkpoint resumed as unattributed; continuing the own-write record through the session's own later calls keeps the peer protection (a peer's edit is not this session's call) without widening the time slack. Topic-named checkpoints were written by sessions and never handed back.

anchors: stamp it from `date` and correct a wrong stamp with the Edit tool, not `sed`
decision: A checkpoint is stamped from `date`, and a wrong stamp in it is corrected with the Edit tool, not sed or another shell edit.

evidence.text: 23 of 25 own checkpoints that resumed as unattributed had been re-stamped with sed right after the clock nudge; the pre-edit skill gave no clock or stamp rule (opus and haiku probes: NONE).

reopen_if: The resume attributes a checkpoint without regard to which tool last changed it, or the clock nudge stops firing on checkpoints.
why: The clock nudge's 'stamp from date in the same command' was read as 'sed -i the stamp with $(date)', and that Bash edit is what broke the resume's attribution of the session's own checkpoint in most of the measured misses; the Edit tool is the route the attribution has always recognised.

anchors: A block saying this session RETIRED its checkpoint
decision: When the resume says this session retired its own checkpoint (it set # STALE or removed the file after writing it, before the compaction), the reader continues from the compaction summary and leaves the file as it is; no save was lost.

evidence.text: 10 of 47 measured misses were self-retired checkpoints; the pre-edit skill had no rule for them (opus and haiku probes: NONE).

reopen_if: A retired checkpoint is shown to hold state the compaction summary lost.
why: Sessions that finished their task before the compaction retired their own checkpoint; the resume called that 'no checkpoint was saved', which read as a lost save and was counted as a miss.

anchors: In plan mode the plan file is the one file you may write.
A block saying the checkpoint is in this session's plan file means you were in plan mode
decision: In plan mode a watcher checkpoint goes into the plan file as its own ## Checkpoint section with its Lessons, the plan left intact; the resume names the plan file, the reader checks its next action against the summary and does not mark it STALE; unfinished items move to OPEN-WORK.md once plan mode ends.

evidence.text: 3 of 47 measured misses were plan-mode sessions; the placement is reasoned from the harness's plan_file_reference attachment, not yet observed in a resumed session. Pre-edit skill: opus and haiku probes NONE.

reopen_if: The user decides a plan-mode checkpoint belongs elsewhere (the scratchpad behind a permission prompt, or no checkpoint at all), or the harness stops attaching the plan file after a compaction.
why: In plan mode the plan file is the only file a session may write, so the save request asked for a handover.md the session could not write; the harness re-attaches the plan file after a compaction, which makes it the one place a checkpoint survives without a permission prompt.
